title: Elon Walking System - Canvas 2D Spec
summary: Complete Canvas 2D walking system for Elon's character. Walk sprites, walkable area, pathfinding, animation. The proof-of-concept that scales to all 13 agents.
content:
Elon Walking System: Canvas 2D Spec

Steffen | 2026-03-17 For Bobby. This is the LAST piece before walking scales to every agent. Elon's server room is the pilot. Get this right, copy to all 13.

What's Delivered

All assets live in projects/steffen/layered-rooms/elon/:

File Type Dimensions Purpose
elon-walk-se.png Sprite strip 384x64 (6 frames) Walk toward camera (primary)
elon-walk-ne.png Sprite strip 384x64 (6 frames) Walk up-right
elon-walk-nw.png Sprite strip 384x64 (6 frames) Walk away from camera
elon-walk-sw.png Sprite strip 384x64 (6 frames) Walk down-left
elon-walk-*.json Metadata -- Animation params per direction
room-background.png Room shell 512x512 RGBA Empty floor + walls
elon-sprite.png Idle pose 512x512 RGBA (sprite ~40x80) Current idle state

Each sprite strip: 6 frames at 64x64px, horizontal, transparent background (PNG-32).

Part 1: Walk Cycle Animation

Sprite Strip Format

Frame layout (left to right):
[F1: Contact R] [F2: Pass+Bounce] [F3: Contact L] [F4: Pass+Bounce] [F5: Contact R] [F6: Pass]
  0px             64px              128px           192px             256px           320px

Each frame is 64x64px. Total strip: 384x64px.

Canvas Draw Call

// Draw one frame of the walk cycle
function drawWalkFrame(ctx, spriteSheet, frameIndex, x, y, scale) {
  const FRAME_W = 64;
  const FRAME_H = 64;

  ctx.drawImage(
    spriteSheet,
    frameIndex * FRAME_W, 0,    // source x, y
    FRAME_W, FRAME_H,           // source width, height
    x - (FRAME_W * scale) / 2,  // dest x (centered)
    y - FRAME_H * scale,        // dest y (feet at y position)
    FRAME_W * scale,             // dest width
    FRAME_H * scale              // dest height
  );
}

Animation Timing

Property Value Notes
Frame duration 150ms 6.67 FPS per frame
Total cycle 900ms 6 frames x 150ms
Bounce frames 2 and 4 (0-indexed: 1, 3) 1px up, already baked into sprites
Walk speed 64px per 900ms 1 grid cell per cycle at 1x scale
Loop Yes Continuous while walking

Direction Selection

When the character moves, choose the sprite strip based on the dominant movement vector in isometric space:

function getWalkDirection(dx, dy) {
  // dx, dy are screen-space deltas (pixels)
  // In isometric 2:1, screen movements map to 4 directions:

  if (dx >= 0 && dy <= 0) return 'ne';  // moving up-right
  if (dx >= 0 && dy > 0)  return 'se';  // moving down-right (toward camera)
  if (dx < 0 && dy <= 0)  return 'nw';  // moving up-left (away from camera)
  if (dx < 0 && dy > 0)   return 'sw';  // moving down-left
}

Rendering with imageRendering

canvas {
  image-rendering: pixelated;
  image-rendering: crisp-edges;
}

This preserves the pixel art crispness at any zoom level. Critical for the Crossy Road feel.

Part 2: Walkable Area (Elon's Server Room)

Room Grid in Isometric Space

Elon's server room occupies grid position { col: 4, row: 3 } in the office floor plan, size { cols: 2, rows: 1 } (128x64 grid units).

The room interior uses 16x16px sub-cells (4x4 per 64px grid cell). Total sub-grid: 8 columns x 4 rows = 32 sub-cells.

Furniture Collision Map

Elon's Room Sub-Grid (8 cols x 4 rows, top-down view):

    Col:  0    1    2    3    4    5    6    7
Row 0:  [    ][    ][ SR ][ SR ][ SR ][ SR ][    ][    ]    SR = Server Rack
Row 1:  [DESK][DESK][ SR ][ SR ][ SR ][ SR ][    ][    ]    DESK = Terminal Desk
Row 2:  [MON ][    ][    ][    ][    ][    ][    ][    ]    MON = Monitor (on desk)
Row 3:  [CHAIR][   ][ .. ][ .. ][ .. ][ .. ][ .. ][    ]    .. = Walkable Floor

Furniture occupying sub-cells:
  Server Racks (x3):  cols 2-5, rows 0-1  (along NE wall)
  Terminal Desk:      cols 0-1, row 1      (NW wall)
  Monitor:            col 0, row 2         (on desk surface, non-blocking)
  Chair:              col 0, row 3         (in front of desk)

Walkable Tiles (Boolean Grid)

// 8x4 grid. true = walkable, false = blocked (furniture or wall)
const ELON_WALKABLE = [
  [false, false, false, false, false, false, false, false],  // Row 0: wall + server racks
  [false, false, false, false, false, false, true,  true ],  // Row 1: desk + racks, floor open right
  [false, true,  true,  true,  true,  true,  true,  true ],  // Row 2: monitor area, open floor
  [false, true,  true,  true,  true,  true,  true,  true ],  // Row 3: chair area then open floor
];

Desk Position (Home/Idle Position)

Elon sits at sub-cell (0, 3) facing SE (toward the terminal). This is his home position. When idle, Elon is here with the idle sprite. When a walk completes, he returns here.

const ELON_HOME = { col: 0, row: 3 };  // Sub-grid coordinates
const ELON_DESK_FACING = 'se';          // Faces terminal

Sub-Cell to Canvas Pixel Conversion

The room renders on a 512x512 canvas. Sub-cells map as follows:

// Convert sub-cell grid position to canvas pixel position
function subCellToCanvas(col, row) {
  // Room interior starts at approximately:
  // Canvas center is (256, 256). Isometric floor diamond.
  // Floor diamond corners (approximate from room-background.png):
  //   Top:    (256, 180)  - north corner of floor
  //   Right:  (430, 310)  - east corner
  //   Bottom: (256, 430)  - south corner
  //   Left:   (80, 310)   - west corner

  // Isometric transform: sub-cell (col, row) maps to:
  const TILE_W = 44;   // half-width of one sub-cell in isometric
  const TILE_H = 22;   // half-height of one sub-cell in isometric
  const ORIGIN_X = 256; // screen center X (top of diamond)
  const ORIGIN_Y = 195; // screen Y of the top corner of the floor diamond

  const screenX = ORIGIN_X + (col - row) * TILE_W;
  const screenY = ORIGIN_Y + (col + row) * TILE_H;

  return { x: screenX, y: screenY };
}

Bobby should fine-tune ORIGIN_X, ORIGIN_Y, TILE_W, TILE_H to align with the actual room-background.png floor diamond. The values above are calculated from the room art.

Part 3: Pathfinding

Algorithm: A* on Sub-Cell Grid

Simple A* pathfinding on the 8x4 walkable grid. Grid is small enough that BFS would also work, but A* gives optimal paths with diagonal support.

class WalkPathfinder {
  constructor(walkableGrid) {
    this.grid = walkableGrid;
    this.rows = walkableGrid.length;
    this.cols = walkableGrid[0].length;
  }

  // Returns array of {col, row} from start to end, or null if no path
  findPath(startCol, startRow, endCol, endRow) {
    // Validate start and end
    if (!this.isWalkable(endCol, endRow)) {
      // Find nearest walkable cell to target
      const nearest = this.nearestWalkable(endCol, endRow);
      if (!nearest) return null;
      endCol = nearest.col;
      endRow = nearest.row;
    }

    const openSet = [{ col: startCol, row: startRow, g: 0, h: 0, f: 0, parent: null }];
    const closedSet = new Set();

    while (openSet.length > 0) {
      // Get node with lowest f
      openSet.sort((a, b) => a.f - b.f);
      const current = openSet.shift();

      if (current.col === endCol && current.row === endRow) {
        // Reconstruct path
        const path = [];
        let node = current;
        while (node) {
          path.unshift({ col: node.col, row: node.row });
          node = node.parent;
        }
        return path;
      }

      closedSet.add(`${current.col},${current.row}`);

      // Check 4 cardinal neighbors (no diagonals for grid walking)
      const neighbors = [
        { col: current.col + 1, row: current.row },
        { col: current.col - 1, row: current.row },
        { col: current.col, row: current.row + 1 },
        { col: current.col, row: current.row - 1 },
      ];

      for (const n of neighbors) {
        if (n.col < 0 || n.col >= this.cols || n.row < 0 || n.row >= this.rows) continue;
        if (!this.grid[n.row][n.col]) continue;
        if (closedSet.has(`${n.col},${n.row}`)) continue;

        const g = current.g + 1;
        const h = Math.abs(n.col - endCol) + Math.abs(n.row - endRow); // Manhattan distance
        const f = g + h;

        const existing = openSet.find(o => o.col === n.col && o.row === n.row);
        if (existing && existing.g <= g) continue;

        openSet.push({ col: n.col, row: n.row, g, h, f, parent: current });
      }
    }

    return null; // No path found
  }

  isWalkable(col, row) {
    if (col < 0 || col >= this.cols || row < 0 || row >= this.rows) return false;
    return this.grid[row][col];
  }

  nearestWalkable(col, row) {
    let best = null;
    let bestDist = Infinity;
    for (let r = 0; r < this.rows; r++) {
      for (let c = 0; c < this.cols; c++) {
        if (!this.grid[r][c]) continue;
        const dist = Math.abs(c - col) + Math.abs(r - row);
        if (dist < bestDist) {
          bestDist = dist;
          best = { col: c, row: r };
        }
      }
    }
    return best;
  }
}

Click-to-Walk Flow

User clicks a spot on the room canvas
  |
  v
Convert canvas pixel (clickX, clickY) to sub-cell (col, row)
  |
  v
Is the target sub-cell walkable?
  |-- No: find nearest walkable sub-cell
  |-- Yes: use as target
  |
  v
Run pathfinder from Elon's current sub-cell to target
  |
  v
Receive path: [{col:0,row:3}, {col:1,row:3}, {col:2,row:3}, ...]
  |
  v
Start walk animation along path

Canvas Click to Sub-Cell Conversion

function canvasToSubCell(clickX, clickY) {
  // Inverse of subCellToCanvas
  // Given screen coordinates, find which sub-cell was clicked

  const TILE_W = 44;
  const TILE_H = 22;
  const ORIGIN_X = 256;
  const ORIGIN_Y = 195;

  // Inverse isometric transform
  const relX = clickX - ORIGIN_X;
  const relY = clickY - ORIGIN_Y;

  // Solve: relX = (col - row) * TILE_W
  //        relY = (col + row) * TILE_H
  const col = Math.round((relX / TILE_W + relY / TILE_H) / 2);
  const row = Math.round((relY / TILE_H - relX / TILE_W) / 2);

  return { col, row };
}

Part 4: Walk Animation Engine

State Machine

IDLE (at desk)
  |
  [click spot or trigger event]
  |
  v
STANDING_UP (2 frames, 200ms)
  |
  v
WALKING (loop walk frames along path)
  |
  [reached destination]
  |
  v
ARRIVING (hold last walk frame, 150ms)
  |
  v
IDLE (at new position, or walking back to desk)

Walk Animation Loop

class ElonWalker {
  constructor(ctx, sprites, pathfinder) {
    this.ctx = ctx;
    this.sprites = sprites;        // { se, ne, nw, sw } loaded Image objects
    this.pathfinder = pathfinder;
    this.state = 'idle';
    this.currentCell = { col: 0, row: 3 };  // Home position
    this.screenPos = subCellToCanvas(0, 3);
    this.path = [];
    this.pathIndex = 0;
    this.frameIndex = 0;
    this.frameTimer = 0;
    this.direction = 'se';
    this.walkSpeed = 64;           // pixels per second (at 1x scale)
    this.frameDuration = 150;      // ms per animation frame
    this.scale = 1.0;              // room zoom scale
  }

  // Called when user clicks a walkable spot
  walkTo(targetCol, targetRow) {
    const path = this.pathfinder.findPath(
      this.currentCell.col, this.currentCell.row,
      targetCol, targetRow
    );

    if (!path || path.length < 2) return;

    this.path = path;
    this.pathIndex = 1;  // Skip start cell (we're already there)
    this.state = 'walking';
    this.frameIndex = 0;
    this.frameTimer = 0;

    // Set initial direction
    this.updateDirection();
  }

  updateDirection() {
    if (this.pathIndex >= this.path.length) return;

    const current = this.path[this.pathIndex - 1];
    const next = this.path[this.pathIndex];

    // Convert grid deltas to screen deltas for direction
    const currentScreen = subCellToCanvas(current.col, current.row);
    const nextScreen = subCellToCanvas(next.col, next.row);

    const dx = nextScreen.x - currentScreen.x;
    const dy = nextScreen.y - currentScreen.y;

    this.direction = getWalkDirection(dx, dy);
  }

  // Called every frame (requestAnimationFrame)
  update(deltaMs) {
    if (this.state !== 'walking') return;

    // Advance animation frame
    this.frameTimer += deltaMs;
    if (this.frameTimer >= this.frameDuration) {
      this.frameTimer -= this.frameDuration;
      this.frameIndex = (this.frameIndex + 1) % 6;
    }

    // Move toward next path node
    const target = this.path[this.pathIndex];
    const targetScreen = subCellToCanvas(target.col, target.row);

    const dx = targetScreen.x - this.screenPos.x;
    const dy = targetScreen.y - this.screenPos.y;
    const dist = Math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);

    const moveAmount = (this.walkSpeed * deltaMs) / 1000;

    if (dist <= moveAmount) {
      // Reached this waypoint
      this.screenPos = { ...targetScreen };
      this.currentCell = { ...target };
      this.pathIndex++;

      if (this.pathIndex >= this.path.length) {
        // Reached destination
        this.state = 'idle';
        this.direction = 'se';  // Face SE when idle
        return;
      }

      // Update direction for next segment
      this.updateDirection();
    } else {
      // Interpolate position
      const ratio = moveAmount / dist;
      this.screenPos.x += dx * ratio;
      this.screenPos.y += dy * ratio;
    }
  }

  draw() {
    if (this.state === 'idle') {
      // Draw idle sprite (or last walk frame facing SE)
      drawWalkFrame(
        this.ctx,
        this.sprites[this.direction],
        0,  // First frame as idle stand
        this.screenPos.x,
        this.screenPos.y,
        this.scale
      );
    } else if (this.state === 'walking') {
      drawWalkFrame(
        this.ctx,
        this.sprites[this.direction],
        this.frameIndex,
        this.screenPos.x,
        this.screenPos.y,
        this.scale
      );
    }
  }
}

Game Loop Integration

// In the main Canvas render loop
let lastTime = performance.now();

function gameLoop(timestamp) {
  const deltaMs = timestamp - lastTime;
  lastTime = timestamp;

  // Clear the room area
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, 512, 512);

  // Layer 1: Room background
  ctx.drawImage(roomBackground, 0, 0);

  // Layer 2: Furniture (server racks, desk, monitor, chair)
  // ... draw furniture sorted by y-position ...

  // Layer 3: Character
  elon.update(deltaMs);
  elon.draw();

  // Layer 4: Light overlay
  // ... green ambient glow ...

  requestAnimationFrame(gameLoop);
}

requestAnimationFrame(gameLoop);

Click Handler

canvas.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
  const rect = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
  const scaleX = canvas.width / rect.width;
  const scaleY = canvas.height / rect.height;

  const canvasX = (e.clientX - rect.left) * scaleX;
  const canvasY = (e.clientY - rect.top) * scaleY;

  const cell = canvasToSubCell(canvasX, canvasY);

  // Only walk to walkable cells within the room
  if (cell.col >= 0 && cell.col < 8 && cell.row >= 0 && cell.row < 4) {
    if (ELON_WALKABLE[cell.row][cell.col]) {
      elon.walkTo(cell.col, cell.row);
    }
  }
});

Part 5: Walk Triggers (Beyond Click)

Walking is not just click-driven. The game triggers walks for agent behaviors:

Trigger Types

Trigger Start End Behavior
Click Current pos Clicked tile Walk there, stay
Status change Desk Nearest server rack Walk to rack, play checking animation, walk back
Handoff receive Door Desk Agent appears at door, walks to desk
Handoff deliver Desk Door Walk to door, disappear (walking to other room)
Error/Death Current pos Door Walk to door, grayscale, disappear
Recovery Door Desk Appear at door, walk to desk
Patrol Desk Random walkable tile Idle behavior: occasionally walks around the room

Door Position

Elon's room has one door on the north wall (shared with Cleo's room):

const ELON_DOOR = { col: 1, row: 0 };  // Sub-cell nearest to door
// The nearest walkable cell to the door:
const ELON_DOOR_WALKABLE = { col: 1, row: 2 };  // Walk to here for door interactions

Patrol Behavior (Idle Animation)

When Elon has been idle for 15+ seconds, occasionally trigger a patrol walk:

function maybePatrol(elon, idleTimeMs) {
  if (idleTimeMs < 15000) return;
  if (Math.random() > 0.02) return;  // 2% chance per frame check (~1x per 8 seconds at 60fps)

  // Pick random walkable tile
  const walkableTiles = [];
  ELON_WALKABLE.forEach((row, r) => {
    row.forEach((cell, c) => {
      if (cell && !(c === elon.currentCell.col && r === elon.currentCell.row)) {
        walkableTiles.push({ col: c, row: r });
      }
    });
  });

  if (walkableTiles.length === 0) return;
  const target = walkableTiles[Math.floor(Math.random() * walkableTiles.length)];
  elon.walkTo(target.col, target.row);

  // After reaching destination, wait 3-5s then walk back to desk
  setTimeout(() => {
    if (elon.state === 'idle' && elon.currentCell.col !== ELON_HOME.col) {
      elon.walkTo(ELON_HOME.col, ELON_HOME.row);
    }
  }, 3000 + Math.random() * 2000);
}

Part 6: Depth Sorting with Furniture

The character must render behind furniture that's "in front" (closer to camera) and in front of furniture that's "behind."

Isometric Depth Rule

In isometric 2:1, depth = col + row. Higher depth = closer to camera = renders later (on top).

function getDepth(col, row) {
  return col + row;
}

// Render order for Elon's room:
// 1. Room background (always first)
// 2. All entities sorted by depth (furniture + character together)
// 3. Light overlay (always last)

function renderRoom(ctx, furniture, character) {
  // Draw room background
  ctx.drawImage(roomBackground, 0, 0);

  // Collect all renderable entities
  const entities = [
    ...furniture.map(f => ({
      type: 'furniture',
      depth: getDepth(f.col, f.row),
      draw: () => ctx.drawImage(f.image, f.x, f.y)
    })),
    {
      type: 'character',
      depth: getDepth(character.currentCell.col, character.currentCell.row),
      draw: () => character.draw()
    }
  ];

  // Sort by depth (ascending = back-to-front)
  entities.sort((a, b) => a.depth - b.depth);

  // Draw all entities
  entities.forEach(e => e.draw());
}

Elon-Specific Depth Notes

  • Server racks (depth 2-6): These are along the NE wall. When Elon walks near them, he should render IN FRONT of racks he's passed (higher row) and BEHIND racks he hasn't reached yet (lower row).
  • Desk (depth 1-2): Against the NW wall. Elon's idle position (depth 3) is in front of the desk.
  • Chair (depth 3): Same depth as Elon's home position. Elon renders on top of chair when seated.

Part 7: Sprite Loading

Asset Loading

async function loadElonWalkSprites() {
  const directions = ['se', 'ne', 'nw', 'sw'];
  const sprites = {};

  const loadImage = (src) => new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const img = new Image();
    img.onload = () => resolve(img);
    img.onerror = reject;
    img.src = src;
  });

  await Promise.all(directions.map(async (dir) => {
    sprites[dir] = await loadImage(`/rooms/elon/elon-walk-${dir}.png`);
  }));

  return sprites;
}

Part 8: Scaling to All 13 Agents

This spec is the template. For each agent:

  1. Walk sprites exist in projects/steffen/sprites/walk/{agent}-walk-{se,ne,nw,sw}.png (all 13 agents, all 4 directions). They're 1024x1024 concept renders that need the same extraction pipeline used here.

  2. Walkable grid differs per room based on furniture layout (see c2-furniture-spec.md for default placements).

  3. Home position is agent-specific (where their desk/chair sits).

  4. Walk personality is defined in c3-walking-sprites-spec.md:

    • Bobby: shuffle, close steps
    • Cleo: bouncy, energetic
    • Alex: slow, deliberate
    • Elon: fastest, utilitarian

    Bobby can implement personality as walkSpeed variation per agent:

    Agent walkSpeed (px/s) Style
    Elon 80 Fastest. No-nonsense.
    Mom 75 Quick, purposeful

    Cleo 70 Bouncy, energetic

  5. Room-to-room walking (inter-room pathfinding) uses the adjacency map from c2-grid-spec.json. That's a separate system Bobby builds on top of this intra-room walking. Each room has a door cell; inter-room walking = walk to door, transition animation, appear at destination room's door, walk to target position.

Part 9: Extraction Pipeline (For Other Agents)

The walk sprites were extracted from 1024x1024 concept renders using background removal + frame slicing. To process all 13 agents:

# From repo root:
python3 scripts/generate-walk-sprites.py  # generates concept renders (already done)
# Then run extraction for each agent (new script needed)
python3 scripts/extract-walk-strips.py    # concept -> canvas-ready strips

The extraction logic:

  1. Open 1024x1024 RGB concept image
  2. Detect background color from corner pixels
  3. Find content regions (non-background clusters)
  4. Divide into frame grid (typically 6x1, 3x2, or 4x2 layout)
  5. Extract each frame, remove background, add alpha
  6. Normalize to 64x64 with bottom-anchor alignment
  7. Apply 1px bounce offset to frames 2 and 4
  8. Compose into 384x64 horizontal strip

The Elon extraction proved this works. Same code generalizes.

Debug Overlay (Development Only)

Bobby should build a debug mode that draws over the room:

function drawDebugOverlay(ctx) {
  // Draw walkable grid
  for (let r = 0; r < 4; r++) {
    for (let c = 0; c < 8; c++) {
      const pos = subCellToCanvas(c, r);
      const color = ELON_WALKABLE[r][c] ? 'rgba(76,175,80,0.2)' : 'rgba(239,68,68,0.15)';

      // Draw isometric diamond for this cell
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.moveTo(pos.x, pos.y - 11);         // top
      ctx.lineTo(pos.x + 22, pos.y);          // right
      ctx.lineTo(pos.x, pos.y + 11);          // bottom
      ctx.lineTo(pos.x - 22, pos.y);          // left
      ctx.closePath();
      ctx.fillStyle = color;
      ctx.fill();
      ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,0.1)';
      ctx.stroke();
    }
  }

  // Draw current path (if walking)
  if (elon.state === 'walking' && elon.path.length > 0) {
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(76,175,80,0.5)';
    ctx.lineWidth = 2;
    ctx.setLineDash([4, 4]);

    const start = subCellToCanvas(elon.path[0].col, elon.path[0].row);
    ctx.moveTo(start.x, start.y);

    for (let i = 1; i < elon.path.length; i++) {
      const p = subCellToCanvas(elon.path[i].col, elon.path[i].row);
      ctx.lineTo(p.x, p.y);
    }
    ctx.stroke();
    ctx.setLineDash([]);
  }

  // Draw home position marker
  const home = subCellToCanvas(ELON_HOME.col, ELON_HOME.row);
  ctx.beginPath();
  ctx.arc(home.x, home.y, 4, 0, Math.PI * 2);
  ctx.fillStyle = '#4CAF50';
  ctx.fill();
}

Toggle with: Ctrl+Shift+D in development, hidden in production.

Summary for Bobby

  1. Load 4 walk sprite strips (384x64 each) + room assets
  2. Build the walkable grid (8x4 boolean array for Elon's room)
  3. Implement A* pathfinding on the grid (copy the class above)
  4. Wire click handler: canvas click -> sub-cell -> pathfind -> walk
  5. Animate at 150ms/frame, 64px/s, direction-based sprite selection
  6. Depth sort character with furniture on every frame
